name: windowed denoising KV rewrite
claim: masked-diffusion-denoising applied to the KV cache so that a bounded trailing window of past key/value entries is iteratively refined by later context before being frozen.
new_capability: the model can correct or sharpen earlier key/value representations using information that arrived after they were written, instead of being stuck with whatever was computed at write-time.
placement: every k decode steps (k a hyperparameter, e.g. 16-64), take the last w KV entries per layer (w << context length), mask/noise a subset of their value vectors, and run 1-4 bidirectional denoising steps conditioned on the surrounding unmasked KV entries in that window only; a small denoiser (shared across layers or per-layer, few hundred K params) is trained jointly with the base model on the same LM objective, with a stop-gradient boundary so future reads use denoised entries but the denoising step itself never reads tokens past the current decode position beyond the fixed window (window is entirely in the past relative to the read that triggers it). Trained from scratch at matched budget alongside a matched-FLOPs vanilla baseline.
invariant: outputs stay causal; because the refreshed entries are always a function of tokens already emitted (the window lags the write head by at least one denoising cycle), no future token's content ever leaks backward into a prediction made before it existed.

name: Barrier-constrained expert routing
claim: Control-barrier-functions applied to the moe-router so that gate logits are projected at inference onto the nearest point of a safety set (e.g. minimum per-expert utilization over a sliding window, or maximum logit gap bound) whenever the raw top-k choice would leave that set, guaranteeing the constraint holds every token without retraining.
new_capability: The system can guarantee, by construction and verifiable at runtime, that no expert is starved or overloaded within any window of W tokens, a property the open-loop router cannot certify because it has no mechanism to correct a choice before it is committed.
placement: Define h(state) = per-expert utilization over the last W tokens minus a floor epsilon; at each step compute the unconstrained top-k logits, then if projected utilization would violate h>=0, solve a small QP (closed-form for top-k, since it's just a logit bias) that minimally perturbs logits to keep h>=0 for the next step. No new trainable parameters; W and epsilon are hyperparameters; runs every token, O(num_experts) extra work.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 MoE, 8 experts, 12 seeds, inject adversarial input distribution shift mid-eval to stress starvation, paperkiln events.jsonl logging

name: Hebbian fast-weight router feedback
claim: Hebbian outer-product fast weights applied to the moe-router gate so that the gate's expert scoring adapts within a sequence based on the expert's recent downstream error, without any gradient step.
new_capability: The router can shift its per-token expert preferences mid-sequence in response to how well recently-chosen experts predicted the actual next tokens, something a static linear gate cannot do at inference.
placement: Add a fast-weight matrix F (same shape as the router's gate weight) updated every token as F <- lambda*F + eta*(outer product of the chosen expert's output error signal and the router's input activation); gate logits become (W + F)x. F is reset per sequence (or decays over a short window of k tokens) and is never checkpointed, only W is trained by backprop as usual. Trained at nano-scale on gpt2-nano with 4-8 experts, top-1 or top-2 routing, comparing perplexity and expert-utilization variance against a matched-FLOPs static router.
invariant: outputs remain causal; the fast-weight update at position t only uses the error/activation from positions <= t, so nothing emitted depends on future tokens.

name: PID-controlled expert capacity
claim: Proportional-integral-derivative feedback control applied to the moe-router so that per-expert capacity thresholds are continuously adjusted to drive measured load imbalance to zero, replacing the static aux-loss weight.
new_capability: The system can maintain expert load balance as a closed-loop control target that adapts online during training (and optionally at inference) instead of relying on a fixed-weight auxiliary loss whose gradient fights the LM loss.

No aux loss gradient is backpropagated for balancing; only Kp/Ki/Kd (few scalars, tuned or fixed) and the router weights via LM loss are involved. name: dual-process router override

name: ARC-policy adaptive merge cache

new_capability: The system can shift which byte n-grams are treated as single tokens mid-stream — collapsing frequently-recurring domain-specific spans (e.g. repeated variable names in a code file) into single-token slots on the fly, and evicting merges that stop being useful, without ever retraining embeddings from scratch.
placement: Maintain a bounded merge-table cache (size fixed to match baseline vocab size) with an ARC-style two-list (recency LRU + frequency LFU, with a ghost-list adaptation parameter) that tracks candidate byte n-grams seen in the current document; every time a candidate's cache hit-count crosses a threshold it is promoted to an active merge and assigned one of a small pool of reserved 'dynamic' embedding slots (their embeddings are looked up by hashing the n-gram, not trained per-item), evicted entries free their slot. This runs once per document at the segmentation stage, before embedding lookup; only the reserved dynamic-slot embedding matrix and the promotion/eviction thresholds are trained (small hash-embedding table, matched param budget by shrinking the static vocab correspondingly).
invariant: outputs remain causal; the ARC cache only ever sees bytes already consumed up to the current position, and promotion decisions for position t depend only on n-grams observed at positions <= t.

falsifier.hypothesis: ARC-adaptive dynamic merging reduces average tokens-per-document and improves perplexity on documents with high local repetition (code, logs) relative to a matched-size static BPE vocabulary, without hurting perplexity on generic prose.
falsifier.metric: perplexity and tokens/byte on held-out code vs. held-out prose, matched vocab+param budget
falsifier.baseline: gpt2-nano preset, static BPE vocab of identical total embedding-table size
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale, 12 seeds, train from scratch at matched FLOPs, evaluate on two held-out domains (repetitive/code, generic prose)

nearest_known: Adaptive/dynamic vocabulary induction (e.g. BPE-dropout, dynamic subword segmentation) combined with ARC cache replacement (Megiddo & Modha)
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

reject_reason: Arithmetic coding compresses a stream to its model's entropy given a fixed probability model; it does not itself decide token boundaries or granularity — it's a downstream lossless coder applied after a distribution is fixed, so it cannot supply variable segmentation at inference. This is just describing standard entropy coding, not a tokenizer redesign.
nearest_known: Arithmetic coding / neural compression with LM priors
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: learned-index dynamic tokeniser
claim: A learned-index model that predicts merge-boundary positions applied to the tokeniser so that segmentation granularity adapts per-span at inference time.
new_capability: The system can locally re-segment easy spans into longer chunks and hard spans into finer pieces at inference, without retraining the base LM's embedding table.
placement: Train a small causal position-predictor (2-layer transformer or GRU, <1M params) on byte offsets that predicts the next merge boundary given only past bytes/tokens; it replaces the static BPE merge lookup with a learned scorer over candidate boundaries. It runs once per byte-window (e.g. every 16 bytes) at both train and inference time, trained jointly with a small auxiliary loss (boundary cross-entropy against BPE merges as a bootstrap target, then fine-tuned against LM loss). The base LM is retrained from scratch at matched FLOPs using the dynamic segmentation, since vocabulary/embedding table changes propagate.
invariant: outputs remain causal; the boundary predictor only ever looks at past bytes/tokens when deciding where to cut, so no future information leaks into segmentation decisions.

falsifier.hypothesis: Dynamic segmentation reduces bits-per-byte on a mixed easy/hard benchmark (e.g. repetitive code vs. rare-word text) versus static BPE at matched FLOPs and params.
falsifier.metric: bits-per-byte on held-out mixed corpus, plus token-count variance across difficulty strata
falsifier.baseline: gpt2-nano preset with standard BPE, matched FLOPs/params
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale (gpt2 preset), 12 seeds, matched token budget (~200M tokens), pre-registered split into easy/hard spans by compressibility

nearest_known: dynamic/entropy-based tokenisation (e.g. Byte Latent Transformer, entropy-based patching) and learned tokenisers like SentencePiece-unigram with adaptive segmentation
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

reject_reason: JIT-tracing specialises a hot execution path for a fixed control-flow graph; it doesn't change segmentation granularity, it caches a computation. Applying it to tokenisation is just caching frequent merge sequences, which is exactly what standard BPE merge-table lookup already does (a static, pre-specialised hot path). No new capability over vanilla BPE.
nearest_known: BPE merge caching / trie-based tokeniser lookup
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: information-bottleneck adaptive chunking
claim: An information-bottleneck objective that explicitly trades off compression of the byte stream against prediction of the next token, applied to the tokeniser, so that chunk boundaries are placed to keep only what predicts the target and discard the rest per-span.
new_capability: The system can vary token length per-span based on an explicit, trained compression-prediction tradeoff (a scalar beta), rather than a fixed frequency-based merge rule, and can be dialed at inference toward more/less compression.
placement: Train a small boundary-scoring network that maximizes I(Z; Y) - beta * I(Z; X) where X is the raw byte window, Z is the induced chunk representation, and Y is the next-token target; implemented as a differentiable relaxation (Gumbel-softmax over boundary positions) trained jointly with a nano LM from scratch. Runs once per fixed byte-window during both training and inference; beta is a hyperparameter swept at test time to show the granularity/performance tradeoff curve.
invariant: outputs remain causal; boundary decisions and the IB objective only condition on bytes up to the current position, never future bytes.

falsifier.hypothesis: IB-trained boundaries yield lower bits-per-byte than static BPE at matched FLOPs, with the compression-prediction tradeoff curve showing a knee that beats fixed vocabulary size choices.
falsifier.metric: bits-per-byte vs. average tokens/byte, sweeping beta
falsifier.baseline: gpt2-nano preset with standard BPE at 2-3 vocab sizes, matched FLOPs
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale, 12 seeds, matched token budget, pre-registered beta grid (5 values)

nearest_known: Information Bottleneck-based segmentation / IB for representation learning (Tishby); analogous to entropy-based patching but with explicit rate term
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: MDL-selected merge depth
claim: A minimum-description-length criterion that scores candidate segmentations by total code length (model bits + data bits) applied to the tokeniser so that merge depth is chosen per-span to minimize total code length rather than by fixed frequency rank.
new_capability: The system can select, per input span, among several precomputed segmentation granularities (e.g. byte/BPE-4k/BPE-32k) the one that minimizes actual total description length under the current model, rather than committing to one vocabulary for the whole corpus.
placement: Precompute 3 candidate segmentations (byte-level, small-BPE, large-BPE) of each training span; at each window (e.g. 64 bytes) compute total code length = -log P(tokens|model) + log(vocab size)*num_tokens under a shared nano LM trained to handle mixed granularity via a granularity-tag token; pick argmin per span. This selection is a discrete search over 3 candidates (cheap), done both at train time (to build a curriculum) and at inference (to pick best segmentation online, causally, using only a short lookahead-free local heuristic since true MDL requires knowing the continuation - approximate by online code length so far). The shared LM is trained from scratch at matched FLOPs across all three granularities jointly.
invariant: outputs remain causal; the MDL selection at inference uses only bits-so-far under each candidate, not future tokens, so the decision is causal (approximate, not exact, MDL).

falsifier.hypothesis: Per-span MDL-selected granularity reduces total bits-per-byte versus any single fixed granularity at matched FLOPs/params.
falsifier.metric: total code length (bits) summed over held-out corpus, decomposed by span type
falsifier.baseline: best single fixed-vocab BPE among the 3 candidates, matched FLOPs
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale, 12 seeds, matched budget, pre-registered span taxonomy (code/prose/numeric)

nearest_known: MDL-based vocabulary induction (e.g. Zipf/MDL BPE variants); multi-granularity/mixed tokenisation with routing
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: RG coarse-graining tokeniser
claim: A renormalisation-group procedure that iteratively coarse-grains adjacent tokens and asks what statistical dependencies survive rescaling, applied to the tokeniser, so that the effective granularity at each layer/position is set by what information survives coarse-graining rather than by a fixed static merge table.
new_capability: The system can build a hierarchy of token representations where each level is defined by what mutual information with the target survives block-averaging, giving a principled multi-scale token pyramid the model can read at different layers instead of one flat vocabulary.
placement: Implement an RG step as: group adjacent token embeddings in blocks of 2-4, apply a learned pooling (like a real-space RG transformation), and keep the pooled representation only if it retains predictive mutual information above a threshold on a held-out slice (measured via a small probe classifier); iterate to build 2-3 coarse-grained levels. Train these pooling operators jointly with a from-scratch nano LM that reads a mix of fine and coarse tokens at different transformer layers (fine tokens at early layers, coarse survivors feed later layers), at matched FLOPs to a flat baseline.
invariant: outputs remain causal; each RG pooling block only combines past tokens within its causal window and coarse tokens are only available once all constituent fine tokens have been seen.

falsifier.hypothesis: Multi-scale RG token pyramid improves long-range dependency modeling (measured by long-context perplexity) versus a flat-vocabulary LM at matched FLOPs/params.
falsifier.metric: perplexity on long-range dependency probes (e.g. induction-head style synthetic tasks, long-document held-out perplexity)
falsifier.baseline: flat BPE gpt2-nano at matched FLOPs/params
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale, 12 seeds, matched budget, pre-registered long-range probe suite

nearest_known: Hierarchical/multi-scale transformers (e.g. MEGABYTE, Funnel Transformer); RG-inspired deep learning theory (Mehta & Schwab) but not previously applied to build a live tokeniser pyramid
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

reject_reason: Importance-sampling corrects an estimator's expectation under distribution mismatch; it is an allocation/reweighting mechanism for samples, not a segmentation mechanism. Applying it to 'granularity' would mean reweighting training examples by inverse tokeniser-induced sampling bias, which does not by construction let the tokeniser vary granularity at inference — it just reweights a fixed static tokenisation's training gradient. The proposed negating op 'allocate' doesn't match the deficit 'static granularity at inference', since IS operates at training-time loss reweighting, not inference-time segmentation.
nearest_known: importance-weighted training / data reweighting for vocabulary imbalance
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

reject_reason: Curriculum-self-paced ordering acts on training example sequencing, not on tokeniser granularity; it has no native mechanism to change segmentation at inference, so it doesn't negate the 'static granularity' deficit — it's a mismatched pairing rather than a testable graft.
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: Multiresolution byte-wavelet embedding
claim: Wavelet-multiresolution decomposition applied to the tokeniser's input embedding stream so that a single forward pass carries both coarse (merged-span) and fine (byte-level) representations simultaneously, letting downstream layers pick resolution per span.
new_capability: The model can represent an easy, predictable span coarsely and a hard, rare span finely within the same sequence without re-tokenising or branching, because both resolutions coexist as additive channels at every position.
placement: Replace the standard subword embedding lookup with a small stack: compute byte-level embeddings, then apply 2-3 levels of a learned Haar-like pooling (average + difference) over fixed windows (e.g. 2, 4, 8 bytes) to produce detail and approximation coefficients; sum the coefficients (with a learned per-level gate) to form the token embedding fed to the existing transformer. Trained end-to-end from scratch at matched param budget (the wavelet filters replace part of the embedding matrix); no change to attention or the causal mask. Runs on paperkiln nano-llama preset, byte-level vocab, matched FLOPs by shrinking embedding dim to compensate for filter params.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the wavelet filters and gating add negligible parameters that are offset by reducing embedding width, and no extra sequence-level computation is introduced so causal masking is untouched.

falsifier.hypothesis: Multiresolution byte-wavelet embeddings reduce bits-per-byte on a mixed easy/hard corpus (e.g. English + rare-word-injected spans) relative to a matched-FLOPs BPE baseline at equal parameter count.
falsifier.metric: bits-per-byte on held-out mixed-difficulty corpus, plus per-span breakdown (easy vs. rare spans defined by unigram frequency)
falsifier.baseline: matched-FLOPs GPT2-nano preset with standard BPE tokeniser, same total params
falsifier.protocol: nano-llama preset, byte-level input, 12 seeds, train to a fixed token budget (e.g. 200M tokens) on paperkiln, matched FLOPs via embedding-dim compensation, report mean+/-std bits-per-byte and per-span breakdown

nearest_known: Byte-level/Charformer-style learned downsampling; wavelet framing is a specific instantiation of multi-scale pooling, close to Perceiver/Charformer soft tokenisation
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

reject_reason: Hebbian fast-weights store transient associations across a few timesteps within a forward pass; they don't natively alter segmentation granularity of a fixed vocabulary, and grafting them onto embeddings collapses to a generic fast-weight attention layer already well studied — no new capability specific to tokeniser adaptivity is produced beyond restating fast-weight memory.
deficit: static: granularity cannot change at inference for easy or hard spans

name: Contrastive merge-embedding co-training
claim: A contrastive objective applied to candidate subword merges during vocabulary construction so that merge selection is driven by which spans the model can predict well jointly with their contexts, rather than by raw co-occurrence frequency.
new_capability: The system can build a vocabulary where merges are chosen to maximise downstream predictive separability (a merged span's embedding is pulled toward its true next-context and pushed from hard negative contexts) instead of being frozen before any model exists.
placement: Run a small auxiliary model (shared with or separate from the main nano-llama) that scores candidate BPE merge pairs by a contrastive loss: embed the merged span and its surrounding context window, pull toward the true continuation embedding and push away from k sampled negative continuations; re-rank merge candidates by this score every N training steps of vocabulary construction (an iterative merge-then-score loop, capped at a few rounds given budget) instead of pure frequency count. Trained from scratch at matched budget: the contrastive scorer is a byte-level bigram encoder trained briefly, then discarded once the vocabulary is frozen; the main model trains normally after on the resulting fixed vocab.
invariant: no retraining of the base model — vocabulary construction happens once, upstream, then the main model trains fresh on the resulting fixed vocabulary exactly as in the baseline pipeline, so this is a from-scratch-at-matched-budget comparison with an added preprocessing stage costed separately.

falsifier.hypothesis: A contrastively-selected merge vocabulary yields lower validation loss / bits-per-token than a frequency-selected BPE vocabulary of identical size, at matched training budget for the main model.
falsifier.metric: validation cross-entropy (bits-per-token) after fixed token budget training
falsifier.baseline: standard frequency-based BPE vocabulary of identical target vocab size (paperkiln default tokeniser)
falsifier.protocol: nano-gpt2 preset, 12 seeds, fixed vocab size (e.g. 8k), build two vocabularies (frequency vs contrastive) on same corpus, train main model to same token budget on each, report mean+/-std final val loss; separately report vocab-construction GPU cost

nearest_known: Predictive/likelihood-driven tokenisation (e.g. unigram LM tokeniser, BPE-dropout, or 'tokenizer-free' contrastive subword induction work); closest is contrastive sentence-piece variants, not a standard shipped method
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

reject_reason: Sequential Monte Carlo requires a per-step likelihood signal to weight and resample hypotheses; applying it to offline vocabulary construction (a one-time discrete combinatorial choice made before the model exists) has no natural resampling dynamics to exploit — this is just 'try several vocabularies and pick the best' relabelled as SMC, which is trivial rather than a genuine mechanism transplant.
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

reject_reason: Kalman filtering fuses a prediction with a noisy measurement online, but tokeniser merge rules are fixed offline before any 'prediction' exists to fuse against; there is no natural state-and-observation pair here, so applying it degenerates to an arbitrary weighted average of two frequency counts, not a genuine feedback correction of merge choice.
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

name: PID-controlled dynamic retokenisation
claim: Feedback control applied to the tokeniser's merge table so that vocabulary composition tracks live model prediction error instead of being frozen from pre-training frequency stats.
new_capability: The system can adapt segmentations mid-training toward units the current model actually struggles to predict, rather than units that were merely frequent in a static corpus scan.
placement: Every N training steps (e.g. every 200), compute per-merge-candidate error signal as the average next-token cross-entropy on sequences containing that byte-pair; maintain a PID loop per candidate merge whose setpoint is a target entropy contribution, with proportional/integral/derivative terms on the error driving a merge-priority score; promote/demote merges into an active vocabulary window of fixed size K when the controller output crosses a threshold. Only the merge-selection controller is trained/updated online; the transformer trains as usual on whatever vocabulary is currently active, with embedding rows for demoted tokens frozen or recycled via mean-init for new ones. Runs on gpt2-nano preset with a small custom tokeniser harness outside paperkiln's C++ trainer, feeding merge updates as periodic vocabulary-swap checkpoints.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the transformer architecture and total embedding budget are held fixed across the run, only which subwords occupy vocabulary slots changes.

falsifier.hypothesis: PID-driven dynamic retokenisation reaches a given validation loss in fewer training tokens than a static BPE vocabulary of the same size.
falsifier.metric: validation cross-entropy at matched token budget
falsifier.baseline: static BPE vocabulary of identical size, same model, same schedule
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano, 12 seeds, 40M token budget, vocabulary swap every 200 steps for first half of training then frozen

nearest_known: BPE-dropout / dynamic vocabulary learning (e.g. VOLT, entropy-based vocabulary learning); not standard PID control but conceptually adjacent
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

reject_reason: Homeostatic plasticity's native operation is normalizing an internal activity statistic (e.g. firing rate) to a setpoint via slow gain scaling — this is just layer-norm/weight-norm territory applied to embeddings, not a mechanism that makes tokenisation prediction-driven. Forcing it onto vocabulary selection is a relabeling of frequency-balancing (already what BPE does) rather than a genuine negation of the deficit.
nearest_known: activation/weight normalization; adaptive softmax frequency binning
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

name: Predictive-error-routed hierarchical tokens
claim: Predictive coding applied to the tokeniser so that a coarse token level only passes a fine-grained byte-level correction signal upward when the coarse prediction fails, letting effective granularity be chosen by prediction error rather than fixed at pre-training time.
new_capability: The system can represent a text span at variable effective resolution decided per-instance by measured predictability, collapsing to single coarse tokens where prediction is easy and expanding to byte-level detail where it is not, without ever re-deriving the vocabulary.
placement: Maintain two lanes: a coarse BPE-token stream and a byte-level stream. A small frozen-schedule coarse LM predicts the next coarse token; wherever its top-1 probability falls below a threshold, the residual (true byte sequence minus what the coarse token implies) is fed to the main model as extra input at that position via a small error-embedding MLP. Trained jointly from scratch at matched budget: the coarse predictor is a small auxiliary head trained alongside the main model on the same data, adding negligible extra parameters. Runs at gpt2-nano/llama-nano scale in paperkiln with byte-level sink lane holding the residual stream.
invariant: outputs stay causal; the error signal at position t is computed only from tokens up to t, and byte-level correction for position t is available before predicting t+1.

falsifier.hypothesis: Error-gated byte augmentation reduces bits-per-byte versus a fixed-vocabulary baseline at matched total parameters and FLOPs, specifically on high-entropy spans (rare words, code).
falsifier.metric: bits-per-byte on held-out mixed text/code corpus, stratified by coarse-token entropy
falsifier.baseline: fixed BPE vocabulary model, same total parameter budget
falsifier.protocol: llama-nano, 12 seeds, 40M token budget, matched FLOPs via reduced main-model width to offset auxiliary head cost

nearest_known: MegaByte / hierarchical byte-level transformers; predictive-coding LMs (e.g. Rao & Ballard-inspired predictive coding networks)
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

reject_reason: Control barrier functions constrain a continuous action to keep a system within a safety set via a real-time forward-invariance certificate; there is no analogous safety set or continuous control variable in vocabulary selection, and forcing it in gives no mechanism beyond 'don't merge tokens that violate constraint X', which is already how blocklisted-merge tokenisers work. Trivial relabeling.
nearest_known: constrained BPE / blocklist merge rules
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

name: Mixture-density boundary prediction
claim: Mixture-density heads applied to the tokeniser's segmentation decision so that token boundaries are drawn from a learned multimodal distribution over segmentation points instead of committed once via greedy frequency merges.
new_capability: The system can maintain and sample multiple plausible segmentations of the same surface string, letting ambiguous spans (e.g. compound words, code identifiers) be scored under several boundary hypotheses rather than being locked to one, and use the mixture's entropy as an uncertainty signal for where tokenisation is unreliable.
placement: A small boundary-predictor network, trained jointly with the LM at matched budget, outputs at each character position a mixture of K Gaussians/categoricals over next-boundary-distance, from which the actual segmentation used for that forward pass is sampled (during training) or taken as the mixture mean (at inference); the LM sees whichever discrete tokens the sampled boundaries imply. Trained from scratch alongside the main model on gpt2-nano preset; only the boundary head's parameters and the resulting discrete tokenisation change per step, main transformer architecture is untouched.
invariant: outputs stay causal; the boundary mixture at position t only conditions on characters up to t, so sampled segmentations never use future characters.

falsifier.hypothesis: Sampling from a learned multimodal boundary distribution during training improves validation loss on morphologically ambiguous test spans versus static BPE at matched FLOPs.
falsifier.metric: validation cross-entropy on a curated ambiguous-compound test split, plus mixture entropy correlation with human-judged ambiguity
falsifier.baseline: static BPE, matched total parameters (boundary head parameters subtracted from main model width)
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano, 12 seeds, 40M tokens, K=3 mixture components

nearest_known: subword regularization / BPE-dropout (stochastic segmentation), and neural segmentation models like Sentence-piece unigram LM; mixture-density heads are borrowed from Bishop's MDN for continuous regression, novel combination here
deficit: frequency-driven merges, not prediction-driven: the vocabulary is chosen before the model exists

name: Conformal recalibration of post-trained logits
claim: Conformal prediction applied to the output head so that after preference post-training, the model emits a calibrated prediction set with a distribution-free coverage guarantee instead of a miscalibrated point-softmax.
new_capability: The system can report, for each generation step, a set of tokens guaranteed to contain the true/reference continuation at a chosen coverage rate under exchangeability, even though the post-trained logits themselves are no longer valid probabilities — enabling downstream abstention or verification decisions that vanilla logits cannot support.
placement: After preference fine-tuning is complete, hold out a calibration set of (context, reference-continuation) pairs; compute nonconformity scores as 1 minus the post-trained model's softmax probability on the reference token; derive the per-token quantile threshold at the target miscoverage rate alpha. At inference, for each step form the prediction set of all tokens whose score is below the threshold; this set is reported alongside (not replacing) the argmax generation. No retraining of the base or post-trained model; only the calibration quantile is fit, on a frozen model, using paperkiln's events.jsonl logits as the score source.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification; the argmax decoding path is untouched, and the conformal set is an auxiliary, verifiable coverage guarantee computed post hoc from held-out calibration data, so base model behavior is never altered — base model untouched.

falsifier.hypothesis: Empirical coverage of the conformal prediction sets on a fresh test split matches the nominal 1-alpha rate within sampling error, whereas raw post-trained softmax top-k sets do not.
falsifier.metric: empirical coverage rate vs nominal 1-alpha, and average prediction-set size
falsifier.baseline: fixed top-k or top-p set from raw post-trained softmax at matched average set size
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano post-trained with a small DPO/preference pass, 12 seeds for calibration-set resampling, calibration set size 2000, test set 2000, alpha=0.1

nearest_known: Conformal language modeling (Quach et al. 2023, conformal prediction sets for LM generation); this is a direct application, not a novel mechanism placement
deficit: after preference post-training the logits are no longer calibrated probabilities

name: Proper-scoring-rule post-hoc recalibration head
claim: A proper scoring rule (CRPS-style / Brier-style loss on a held-out calibration split) applied to the output-head so that the post-preference-trained logits recover calibrated probabilities without touching the base weights.
new_capability: The system can report confidence scores after RLHF/DPO-style tuning that match empirical outcome frequencies, enabling correct downstream use of log-probabilities (e.g. for selective abstention or reranking), which the vanilla post-trained model cannot do because its logits are systematically over/under-confident.
placement: Freeze the preference-tuned model; add a small affine or temperature/vector-scaling transform (a handful of parameters per vocabulary bucket or a single temperature) on top of final logits; train this transform by minimizing a strictly proper scoring rule (e.g. multiclass Brier or log-score) on a held-out labeled continuation set (next-token identity as outcome), computed once, offline, after post-training finishes. Only the small calibration map is trained; base model is untouched.
invariant: base model untouched

falsifier.hypothesis: Post-hoc scoring-rule calibration reduces expected calibration error (ECE) of next-token probabilities after preference tuning without degrading task accuracy/perplexity beyond noise.
falsifier.metric: ECE (binned) and negative log-likelihood on held-out validation tokens; downstream task accuracy delta
falsifier.baseline: raw preference-tuned logits (no calibration) and standard temperature scaling
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2-preset trained then DPO-style toy preference finetune on paperkiln, 12 seeds, matched FLOPs, calibration map fit on 5% held-out split, evaluate ECE/NLL on disjoint test split

nearest_known: Temperature scaling (Guo et al. 2017) / Platt scaling
deficit: after preference post-training the logits are no longer calibrated probabilities

reject_reason: Speculate-and-verify negates a *sampling-cost* deficit (needing many exact forward passes), not a *calibration* deficit; verifying against the exact computation says nothing about whether the exact computation's probabilities are calibrated. This is a category mismatch — it's just speculative decoding relabeled, and it doesn't touch calibration at all.
nearest_known: Speculative decoding (Leviathan et al. 2023, Chen et al. 2023)
deficit: after preference post-training the logits are no longer calibrated probabilities

name: Energy-based candidate refinement head
claim: An energy-based refinement procedure applied to the output-head so that the final token distribution is produced by iterative descent over a learned energy on (context, candidate) pairs rather than a single softmax read, yielding better-calibrated aggregate probabilities than the raw post-trained logits.
new_capability: The system can trade extra inference-time compute for a distribution over next tokens whose top-k mass better reflects empirical correctness rates, something a single fixed-temperature softmax read cannot do because it has no mechanism to revise its own confidence using multiple candidate evaluations.
placement: Train a small scalar energy function E(context_repr, candidate_token_repr) as a lightweight head (2-layer MLP) on top of frozen preference-tuned hidden states; at inference, sample a candidate set from the base logits, score each by softmax(-E), take several gradient/Langevin refinement steps on the energy over a continuous relaxation of candidate embeddings, then re-snap to nearest vocabulary token via the frozen unembedding; train the energy head with a contrastive loss (real next-token vs. sampled negatives) on the training corpus, base model frozen.
invariant: base model untouched

falsifier.hypothesis: Energy-based refinement reduces ECE and improves selective-prediction risk-coverage compared to raw logits, at matched extra-FLOPs budget for K refinement steps.
falsifier.metric: ECE, NLL, risk-coverage AUC at K in {1,4,8} refinement steps
falsifier.baseline: raw preference-tuned softmax; nucleus sampling with same extra FLOPs spent on more samples instead of refinement
falsifier.protocol: nano llama preset, 12 seeds, matched FLOPs (extra compute budget equalized against baseline resampling), paperkiln events.jsonl logging of ECE per step

nearest_known: Energy-based models for structured prediction / EBM rerankers (LeCun et al.; residual energy-based models, Bakhtin et al. 2021)
deficit: after preference post-training the logits are no longer calibrated probabilities

name: Kalman-fused logit calibration
claim: Kalman filtering applied to the output-head so that the preference-tuned logits (a noisy 'measurement') are fused at inference time with a pretrained-base-model prediction (the 'prior') in proportion to each source's estimated uncertainty, restoring calibration lost during preference tuning.
new_capability: The system can produce per-token probability estimates that automatically down-weight the preference-tuned model wherever it is over-confident and up-weight the original pretrained distribution, something neither model alone can do since neither carries an explicit uncertainty estimate about itself.
placement: Run the frozen base (pre-preference) model and the frozen preference-tuned model in parallel over the same context at every generation step (or every k tokens for efficiency); treat base logits as the 'prediction' and preference-tuned logits as the 'measurement', maintain a running estimate of each model's calibration variance (learned scalar or class-conditional variance from a small held-out set), and fuse the two logit vectors via a Kalman-style weighted average (in logit space) with weights set by the inverse variances. Only the variance/gain parameters are trained (small, offline, on a calibration split); both LMs are untouched.

placement: At each decoding step t, run n=4-8 forward passes over the same causal prefix with small input-embedding dropout/noise perturbations (or n cached KV variants), producing a trajectory of logit vectors; maintain an exponential moving average of these logits with decay beta tuned on a held-out set, and sample/argmax from the EMA logits to commit token t. No new parameters are trained beyond possibly tuning beta; the base model is untouched, this is purely an inference-time procedure layered on the existing sampler loop in paperkiln.
invariant: outputs remain causal; each of the n perturbed forward passes only conditions on the already-committed causal prefix (tokens < t), so averaging their logits does not leak information from future tokens, and no token is emitted before its position.

falsifier.hypothesis: EMA-averaged multi-pass logits reduce next-token error rate / improve calibration (ECE) vs single-pass logits at matched inference FLOPs (by comparing against an n-times-wider single model of equal total FLOPs).
falsifier.metric: perplexity, expected calibration error, and wall-clock cost ratio
falsifier.baseline: single deterministic forward pass sampler on matched-FLOPs gpt2-nano (widened to match the n-fold compute of the EMA variant)
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 12 seeds, sweep n in {2,4,8} and beta in {0.5,0.7,0.9}, report perplexity/ECE with pre-registered improvement threshold over matched-FLOPs baseline

nearest_known: self-ensembling / test-time augmentation and stochastic weight/logit averaging (Polyak-Ruppert averaging, SWA); not a standard decoding-loop technique in LMs, but conceptually close to test-time MC-dropout ensembling
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: energy-descent candidate refinement sampler
claim: Energy-based-refinement applied to the sampler so that, instead of sampling a token once from the softmax, the system samples a small candidate set, scores it with a learned scalar energy function conditioned on the causal context, and performs a few gradient or hill-climbing steps over an embedding relaxation before snapping to the nearest vocabulary token, still emitting one committed token per position.
new_capability: The sampler can correct locally implausible token choices (e.g. ones that are locally high-probability but globally incoherent with recent context) by optimizing a learned compatibility energy over a short candidate list before committing, which single-shot softmax sampling structurally cannot do since it never revisits a draft before emission.
placement: Train a small energy head E(h_t, e(v)) — an MLP taking the causal hidden state h_t and a candidate token embedding — via contrastive noise-conditional training (real next-token embeddings as low-energy, corrupted/random vocabulary embeddings as high-energy), on the same training corpus as the base LM, at matched FLOPs by trimming base model depth. At inference for each position: draw top-k candidates from the base softmax, run 3-5 steps of gradient descent on the energy over a continuous relaxation of the candidate embeddings (Gumbel-softmax style), then project back to the nearest discrete token in the top-k set and commit it as the single output token for that position.
invariant: outputs remain causal; the energy descent only reorders/reweights candidates drawn from the causal softmax at the current position t using hidden state h_t which depends only on tokens < t, and only one token is committed per position, so no future information is used and generation remains strictly left-to-right.

falsifier.hypothesis: Energy-descent refinement over top-k candidates improves sample quality (lower perplexity of held-out human text under the energy-corrected distribution, or higher human/automatic coherence score) versus plain top-k softmax sampling at matched FLOPs and matched wall-clock candidate count.
falsifier.metric: perplexity under corrected distribution, MAUVE or n-gram coherence score vs reference continuations, wall-clock cost overhead
falsifier.baseline: top-k softmax sampling on matched-FLOPs gpt2-nano (energy head FLOPs offset by trimming base model)
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 12 seeds, k in {10,20,50}, 3-5 energy descent steps, report metrics with pre-registered improvement threshold vs baseline top-k sampling

nearest_known: energy-based text generation / COLD decoding (Qin et al. 2022); Gumbel-softmax relaxation refinement for discrete sampling
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: Hopfield draft-block retrieval
claim: Hopfield energy-descent retrieval over a memory bank of stored n-gram/hidden-state patterns applied to the sampler so that a block of draft tokens can be produced in one associative-recall step instead of one forward pass per token
new_capability: The sampler can propose multiple future tokens per step by converging a Hopfield energy descent over cached activation patterns, rather than emitting exactly one token per forward pass.
placement: At each decoding step, take the current hidden state as a query, run 3-5 steps of modern-Hopfield energy descent (softmax-weighted attention over a fixed bank of stored (context-embedding, continuation) pairs mined from training data) to retrieve a converged pattern, decode it into a k-token draft block, then verify the block causally with one real forward pass (as in speculative decoding) and accept the causal prefix. The Hopfield memory bank is trained/fitted once offline (k-means or gradient fit of stored patterns) at nano-scale on the same corpus; the base LM is untouched.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

falsifier.hypothesis: Hopfield-retrieved draft blocks have higher acceptance rate under exact verification than a matched-size n-gram or small-LM drafter at equal draft-model FLOPs.
falsifier.metric: tokens-accepted-per-verification-pass; wall-clock tokens/sec at matched total FLOPs
falsifier.baseline: standard speculative decoding with a small transformer drafter, matched parameter/FLOP budget for the retrieval bank vs drafter
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 12 seeds, fixed 40k-token eval set, memory bank size matched in FLOPs to drafter model, report mean+-std acceptance rate

nearest_known: Speculative decoding with a retrieval-based drafter (e.g. REST / retrieval-augmented speculative decoding)
_note: This is essentially speculative decoding with a Hopfield-network drafter; the 'denoise' framing is decorative. Coherent but not novel beyond swapping drafter architecture.
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

reject_reason: Population-based hypothesis weighting with resampling over token sequences, applied to autoregressive decoding, is standard particle-filter / SMC decoding already explored for constrained/controlled generation; combined with the stated 'speculate' negating op this collapses into speculative decoding with multiple candidate sequences, which is an existing method under a new name, not a new mechanism against the sequential deficit.
nearest_known: Sequential Monte Carlo steering / particle-filter decoding (e.g. SMC for LM control, Lew et al.)
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: Kalman-fused draft correction
claim: Kalman-style fusion of a fast low-fidelity token-block predictor (prediction) with a slower exact forward pass (measurement), weighted by their calibrated uncertainties, applied to the sampler so that multiple tokens can be committed per exact forward pass without waiting for full sequential confirmation
new_capability: The sampler can emit a block of tokens by blending a cheap draft distribution with an exact-model distribution in proportion to each one's estimated variance, rather than requiring one full forward pass to commit each token.

Only the small variance head is trained (nano-scale, few hours); base model is untouched.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

falsifier.hypothesis: Kalman-fused sampling reduces perplexity-matched wall-clock generation time versus plain speculative decoding at equal correction frequency k, because the variance-weighted fusion accepts more draft tokens than raw argmax draft acceptance.
falsifier.metric: tokens/sec at fixed downstream perplexity/accuracy; acceptance rate of draft tokens before correction
falsifier.baseline: vanilla speculative decoding (accept/reject, no soft fusion) at matched k and matched drafter size
falsifier.protocol: llama-nano preset, 12 seeds, k in {4,8,16}, matched FLOPs for drafter+variance head vs plain drafter, report tokens/sec and exact-match perplexity

nearest_known: Speculative decoding; soft/weighted speculative sampling variants (e.g. Medusa's tree verification, SpecInfer)
_note: Kalman fusion is a genuine addition (uncertainty-weighted blending instead of hard accept/reject) but it's an incremental variant of speculative decoding rather than a structural break of sequentiality.
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: Spectral block decoding
claim: A frequency-basis transform (e.g. short-time DCT/FFT over token-embedding trajectories) applied to the sampler so that a block of future token representations can be generated by extrapolating low-frequency spectral coefficients in parallel, instead of one autoregressive step per token
new_capability: The sampler can predict a whole block of upcoming token embeddings at once by extrapolating a small number of low-frequency spectral coefficients, then invert-transform and decode them in parallel, rather than being forced to emit tokens one at a time.

Only the spectral predictor head is trained at nano-scale; base LM untouched.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

falsifier.hypothesis: Spectral extrapolation of embedding trajectories yields higher block-acceptance rate under exact verification than a same-size autoregressive drafter, because low-frequency coefficients of natural text embeddings are more predictable than raw next-token identity.
falsifier.metric: accepted-tokens-per-verification-step; spectral-predictor FLOPs vs autoregressive-drafter FLOPs at matched acceptance
falsifier.baseline: speculative decoding with matched-FLOP autoregressive small-transformer drafter
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano, 12 seeds, block size k in {4,8,16}, fixed eval corpus, report acceptance rate and tokens/sec

nearest_known: Non-autoregressive / spectral generation methods in other modalities (e.g. FNet-style mixing, spectral speech vocoders); no direct LM decoding precedent found
_note: Genuinely distinct mechanism (frequency-domain block prediction rather than time-domain drafting) — worth keeping despite low feasibility.
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: Predictive-coding residual sampler
claim: A hierarchical predictive-coding loop that propagates only prediction errors between a fast shallow drafting stack and a slow deep verifying stack, applied to the sampler so that most decoding steps only need a cheap error-update rather than a full deep forward pass
new_capability: The sampler can commit tokens using a fast shallow-layer prediction most of the time, only invoking full-depth computation to correct residual error when the shallow prediction's error signal exceeds a threshold, reducing full-model forward passes below one-per-token.

At each step, the shallow stack produces a draft logit and a scalar/error-vector signal for how much the deep layers would change it, estimated by an auxiliary error-predictor head trained to regress the shallow-vs-full logit divergence; when predicted error is below threshold, sample from the shallow logit alone (skipping deep layers, cached from previous step where valid); when above threshold, run the full stack and propagate the correction. Only the small error-predictor head is trained; base LM layers untouched, effectively early-exit gated by a learned predictive-coding signal instead of a fixed confidence threshold.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

falsifier.hypothesis: Gating full-depth computation by a trained error-prediction signal (rather than plain softmax-confidence early exit) reduces average FLOPs per token at matched perplexity.
falsifier.metric: average FLOPs/token at fixed perplexity degradation tolerance (e.g. <=0.5 nats)
falsifier.baseline: standard confidence-based early-exit with matched exit-head budget
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano and llama-nano, 12 seeds, sweep error threshold, matched extra-parameter budget for error head vs confidence head

nearest_known: Early-exit transformers (e.g. DeeBERT, CALM) — this is a relabeling of early-exit gated by a learned error signal rather than confidence, which the prompt explicitly flags as a bad move
_reject_consideration: Borderline: kept as not-reject because the error-signal-vs-confidence-signal distinction is a real, testable difference, but it is close to the disallowed 'early exit under new name' pattern.
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

reject_reason: Adding redundancy to detect/repair corruption is a channel-coding idea about robustness to noise, not about breaking sequential dependency; applied to a sampler with the 'denoise' op it just becomes error-correcting output codes for speculative-decoding verification, i.e. a description of the existing accept/reject verification step in speculative decoding relabeled as ECC, with no new mechanism-negates-deficit relationship established.
nearest_known: Speculative decoding verification step / redundant-check decoding
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

reject_reason: This is speculative decoding under a different name: branch-prediction-from-history plus speculative proceed is exactly draft-then-verify decoding, already standard.
nearest_known: Speculative decoding (Leviathan et al. 2023, Chen et al. 2023)

name: transactional multi-token commit blocks
claim: transactions-and-rollback applied to the sampler so that groups of speculatively generated tokens commit atomically or abort as a whole, exposing an explicit commit boundary the model can condition future speculation width on
new_capability: The system can adapt its speculation batch size online based on a learned per-position abort-rate signal, rather than using a fixed or heuristic draft length as in vanilla speculative decoding.
placement: At each step, draft K tokens with a small draft model or n-gram cache, then verify all K in one forward pass of the target model; instead of accepting only the longest exact-match prefix (standard rejection sampling), log a per-position 'transaction log' (accept/abort bitmap plus the logit divergence) to events.jsonl and train a tiny auxiliary head (logistic regression over draft-model entropy and position index) to predict the optimal K for the next block. Only the predictor is trained; the base model is untouched. Runs on paperkiln's exact-attention lane with a nano draft model built from the same tokenizer.
invariant: exactness is recoverable: rejection sampling guarantees the committed sequence is distributed identically to greedy/sampled decoding from the target model alone, since aborted tokens are discarded and regenerated exactly.

falsifier.hypothesis: Learned adaptive K reduces mean forward-pass count per accepted token by >=15% versus fixed-K speculative decoding at equal acceptance-rate distribution.
falsifier.metric: forward passes per emitted token; wall-clock tokens/sec
falsifier.baseline: fixed-K speculative decoding (K=4) matched FLOPs, same draft model
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2-small target + nano draft model, 12 seeds, 3 prompt distributions (in-domain, OOD, code), matched wall-clock budget on one L4

nearest_known: Speculative decoding with adaptive draft length (e.g. SpecDec++, dynamic speculation depth papers)
deficit: strictly sequential: one token per forward pass

name: diffusion patch-repair over committed spans
claim: masked-diffusion-denoising applied to the sampler so that a fixed trailing window of already-committed tokens can be jointly re-masked and re-denoised using bidirectional context from tokens generated after them, before being permanently frozen
new_capability: The system can correct locally incoherent earlier tokens (e.g. wrong entity, broken agreement) using information only available after they were emitted, something a strictly autoregressive sampler cannot do by construction.
placement: Every k=16 committed tokens, re-mask the last w=8 tokens, run 2-4 diffusion denoising steps conditioned on both the preceding fixed prefix and the w tokens' own bidirectional context (a small side network sharing embeddings with the base LM), then commit the denoised window permanently; only the denoiser side-network is trained, base LM frozen. Implemented as a second attention lane in paperkiln reusing the sliding-window lane's KV slice.
invariant: streaming: the denoiser only ever revises within a bounded trailing window that has not yet been read by any downstream consumer/output stream, so token-by-token emission to the outside world is delayed by exactly w tokens but never depends on future input beyond that fixed lag.

falsifier.hypothesis: Windowed diffusion repair reduces per-token perplexity on the delayed output stream by >=5% versus pure autoregressive decoding at matched FLOPs (denoiser FLOPs charged against the budget).
falsifier.metric: perplexity of final committed sequence; edit rate (fraction of tokens changed) vs downstream quality gain
falsifier.baseline: matched-FLOPs autoregressive nano-gpt2 with equivalent extra forward passes spent on more autoregressive steps instead
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano preset, 12 seeds, w in {4,8,16}, k in {8,16,32} grid, held-out wikitext-nano slice

nearest_known: Semi-autoregressive/insertion diffusion decoding (e.g. SUNDAE, CMLM, block diffusion LMs)
deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

name: fast-weight overwrite of committed token memory
claim: delta-rule-memory applied to the sampler so that a committed token's contribution to a separate associative fast-weight state can be erased and overwritten by later context, without altering the emitted token sequence itself
new_capability: The system can revise its internal belief about what an earlier committed token 'meant' (its associative value read by later attention) without violating causality of the emitted symbol stream, giving a form of soft semantic rollback vanilla KV-cache attention cannot express.
placement: Maintain a fast-weight matrix S (key->value associative memory) updated at every step with the delta rule S_t = S_{t-1} + k_t(v_t - S_{t-1}^T k_t)^T using the same key as the token's original KV entry; a small linear read head mixes standard causal attention output with a read from S at each query. Only the delta-rule head and mixing gate are trained on top of a frozen base LM (graft).
invariant: outputs stay causal: the delta-rule update at step t only uses k_t, v_t, and past state, and the read at step t only queries state built from tokens <= t, so nothing emitted depends on future tokens.

falsifier.hypothesis: Adding delta-rule associative memory improves long-range coreference accuracy (synthetic key-value recall task) by >=10 points over frozen-base + linear-attention baseline at matched added parameters.
falsifier.metric: exact-match accuracy on synthetic overwrite-recall probe (store key K with value A, later restore same key with value B, query K)
falsifier.baseline: frozen base LM + standard linear attention head of equal parameter count, no delta rule
falsifier.protocol: llama-nano preset, 12 seeds, probe sequence lengths {128,512,2048}, matched added-parameter budget

nearest_known: DeltaNet / fast-weight programmers (Schlag et al., Yang et al. DeltaNet)
deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

name: conformal per-token abstention bands
claim: conformal-prediction applied to the sampler so that each committed token carries a distribution-free guaranteed-coverage confidence set, letting downstream consumers or a rollback controller detect exactly which committed tokens are statistically unreliable
new_capability: The system can flag, with a calibrated distribution-free guarantee, which already-emitted tokens are likely wrong and trigger targeted re-generation of only those spans, rather than treating all committed tokens as equally final.
placement: On a held-out calibration set, compute nonconformity scores (1 - softmax prob of true continuation) and derive a threshold q_hat for target coverage 1-alpha; at inference, for each generated token build the conformal set {tokens with cumulative prob >= 1-q_hat} and record set size / whether the emitted token is a low-margin member to events.jsonl. A controller (rule-based, no training) triggers windowed re-decoding (using the diffusion-repair or plain re-sampling) only where set size exceeds a threshold. No base model training; only calibration.
invariant: exactness is recoverable: conformal calibration is a post-hoc statistical wrapper computed from a held-out calibration set and does not alter model weights, so the exact base-model distribution is always recoverable by ignoring the sets.

falsifier.hypothesis: Flagging tokens via conformal set size and selectively re-decoding them reduces downstream factual-error rate by >=10% at <=20% extra compute versus uniform re-decoding of the same total token budget.
falsifier.metric: factual/format error rate on a synthetic slot-filling task; extra forward passes spent
falsifier.baseline: uniform random re-decoding of the same fraction of tokens, matched compute
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano, 12 seeds, alpha in {0.05,0.1,0.2}, calibration set 2k examples held out

nearest_known: Conformal language modeling / conformal prediction sets for LLM outputs (Quach et al. 2024, Kumar et al. conformal decoding)
deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

reject_reason: Speculate-and-verify with rollback against exact computation is definitionally speculative decoding; applying it to negate 'no rollback' just re-describes the same standard mechanism already covered by the sampler's usual accept/reject step.
nearest_known: Speculative decoding (Leviathan et al. 2023)
deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

name: energy-descent block resampling
claim: energy-based-refinement applied to the sampler so that a committed block of tokens can be revised before being finalized rather than accepted token-by-token forever
new_capability: the system can locally undo and rewrite a just-generated span when a cheap energy score flags it as low quality, instead of being stuck with the first sampled continuation
placement: after generating a block of N tokens (e.g. N=8) with the normal autoregressive sampler, treat the block as a candidate and run K steps of Langevin-style or iterative denoising descent on an energy function (e.g. negative log-likelihood under the same model plus an auxiliary discriminator) over the block's soft token embeddings or over a small discrete neighborhood (swap/mask-and-refill moves); only the descended block is committed, and generation then proceeds causally from there. Trained: an optional lightweight energy head (a 2-layer MLP on top of frozen backbone hidden states) trained with contrastive samples (real continuation vs resampled), separate from the base LM.
invariant: exactness recoverable: the block-level refinement is always checked against a verification pass (log-prob under base model must not decrease vs raw sample; if it does, revert to raw sample) so the exact greedy/sampled baseline output is recoverable as a fallback

falsifier.hypothesis: block energy-descent refinement improves perplexity/quality per generated token at equal or lower wall-clock decoding budget vs plain sampling with the same number of forward passes
falsifier.metric: held-out perplexity of refined vs raw continuations, and win-rate under a fixed automatic quality proxy (e.g. reverse-model log-likelihood)

falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 12 seeds, block size 8, K in {2,4,8} descent steps, compare against best-of-K sampling at same total FLOPs, report mean+CI

nearest_known: discrete Langevin / energy-based text infilling (e.g. COLD decoding, Mirostat is not this, closer to Lu et al. COLD Decoding 2022)
deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

name: SMC particle decoding
claim: sequential-monte-carlo applied to the sampler so that multiple candidate continuations are tracked and reweighted in parallel, letting low-weight hypotheses be dropped and replaced rather than committing to a single irrevocable token
new_capability: the system can maintain and prune a population of partial hypotheses so that a token choice that looks good locally but leads to a bad continuation gets discarded a few steps later via resampling, which single-path ancestral sampling cannot do
placement: maintain P particles (each a partial token sequence + running weight from an importance function like exponentiated future log-prob under short lookahead or a cheap reward model); at each step extend all particles by one token, update weights, and resample (systematic resampling) every R steps; particles resampled away are discarded, survivors are copied. Trained: nothing new needs training if the weight function is the base model's own log-prob (bootstrap SMC), otherwise a small learned twist function trained via self-normalized importance sampling on held-out sequences.
invariant: outputs remain causal: each particle's extension only ever conditions on its own already-generated prefix, resampling only changes which prefixes survive, never injects future information into a token's logits

falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, P in {4,8,16}, resample every R in {4,8}, 12 seeds, report predicate satisfaction rate and perplexity with CIs

name: evolutionary beam mutation decoding
claim: evolutionary-population applied to the sampler so that a population of candidate continuations is mutated and selected across generations, allowing a previously committed span to be replaced by a mutated descendant that scores better under a fitness function

falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, M in {8,16}, G in {2,4,8}, mutation span L in {4,8}, 12 seeds

deficit: no rollback: a committed token is never revised

name: checksum-verified token repair

name: arithmetic-coded reversible sampler

new_capability: the system can retroactively re-rank or re-derive alternate continuations from the exact same underlying random stream (the arithmetic-coding tape), enabling bit-exact replay and counterfactual re-sampling of a generation under a different top-p/temperature without re-running the forward pass from scratch.
placement: At each decode step, instead of sampling a token directly from the softmax, map the model's CDF onto the current arithmetic-coding interval and record the interval bounds and the raw code-stream bits consumed; store this per-token receipt in events.jsonl. Off-line, a decoder can replay the same bits through a different (but calibrated) probability assignment to deterministically recover alternate token choices, giving an exact bijection between random bits and tokens. Nothing is trained; this is a bookkeeping/encoding layer added around the existing sampler in paperkiln, tested on gpt2-nano at matched FLOPs (encode/decode overhead is O(vocab) per step, already paid by the softmax).
invariant: exactness is recoverable: the arithmetic code is a bijection between bitstreams and token sequences under the recorded model distribution, so the original sample can always be exactly reconstructed from the stored bits.

falsifier.baseline: standard multinomial sampling with stored PRNG seed only (no arithmetic coding)
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano, 12 seeds, 500 generations of 256 tokens each, matched FLOPs, compare reconstruction fidelity and re-sampling diversity

name: transactional multi-token commit sampler
claim: transactions-and-rollback applied to the sampler so that a block of k tokens is generated speculatively as an uncommitted transaction and only committed atomically if a post-hoc verifier accepts the whole block, otherwise the entire block is discarded and regenerated
new_capability: the system can undo a run of already-emitted tokens when a cheap downstream check (e.g. a constraint parser, a small reward model, or a coherence score) fails, rather than being forced to accept every token as permanent the instant it is produced.
placement: Generate blocks of k tokens (k=4-8) under the base model without emitting them externally; run a lightweight verifier (rule-based constraint checker, or a distilled scorer trained separately from the base model) over the completed block; if it passes, atomically append the block to the committed output and KV cache, else roll back the KV cache to the pre-block checkpoint and resample the block (bounded retries). Only the verifier is trained (small classifier on nano-scale data); base model is untouched. Implemented in paperkiln as a checkpoint/restore of the KV cache state around a rejection-sampling loop over blocks.
invariant: outputs remain causal: nothing is emitted to the outside world until its enclosing block is verified, so no user-visible token is ever generated conditioned on a future token, and rollback only discards not-yet-externalized tokens.

falsifier.baseline: nucleus sampling with no rollback, same base model and same total sampling budget (including retry cost given as extra forward passes)
falsifier.protocol: gpt2-nano and llama-nano, 12 seeds, synthetic constrained-generation task, matched FLOPs including retries, block size swept in {4,8,16}

new_capability: The optimiser can share statistical structure about gradient-noise patterns across parameters within the same module type (e.g. all attention Q-projections) via a learned dictionary, letting new/rare parameters inherit sensible second-moment estimates from the dictionary rather than starting from per-parameter zero-history, and letting moment storage compress module-wise.
placement: Maintain, per module class (e.g. per attention head, per MLP layer), a small dictionary of K atoms (each shaped like the flattened per-parameter moment vector for that module) updated by online sparse coding (matching-pursuit or Adam-friendly proximal update) every N optimiser steps using the current raw second-moment estimates as the signal to encode; the Adam update then reads the moment as (reconstructed dictionary combination) instead of the raw exponential moving average, with the residual kept and injected back to preserve exactness. Dictionary atoms and sparse codes are trained/updated online alongside the model, adding a small number of extra parameters (K atoms × atom-dim per module class) and a cheap sparse-coding step.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification: the raw per-parameter EMA moment is still tracked as the residual/ground truth alongside the sparse reconstruction, so at any checkpoint the exact standard-Adam trajectory can be restored by falling back to raw moments if the sparse approximation underperforms.

falsifier.hypothesis: Sparse-coded shared moments reduce loss variance / speed convergence versus per-parameter Adam moments at matched FLOPs, particularly early in training when per-parameter statistics are noisy.
falsifier.metric: training loss at fixed step count, wall-clock to target perplexity, gradient-noise-adjusted convergence curve
falsifier.baseline: vanilla Adam moments, matched param count including dictionary overhead counted against baseline's implicit larger batch
falsifier.protocol: nano llama preset, paperkiln, 12 seeds, matched FLOPs (dictionary maintenance cost budgeted in), 40 GPU-hour budget, ablate dictionary size K

nearest_known: Shampoo/K-FAC structured second-moment approximations; factored Adafactor moments; dictionary learning for optimizer states is novel to our knowledge
deficit: per-parameter and structureless: the moments know nothing of the module they belong to

name: Spectral optimiser-moment sharing
claim: Spectral-transform applied to per-parameter optimiser moments so that second-moment statistics for weight matrices are tracked in a frequency basis (2D DCT/FFT over the weight matrix's row/column index) where long-range correlations between distant parameters in the same module become local and can be captured by a small number of low-frequency coefficients.
new_capability: The optimiser can capture correlated noise/curvature structure across an entire weight matrix (not just per-scalar-parameter) using O(few) shared low-frequency coefficients instead of one independent moment per parameter, giving structured preconditioning that generalizes across rows/columns of the same module without the O(d^2) cost of full second-order methods.
placement: For each 2D weight tensor, maintain the standard elementwise second moment plus a small set of low-frequency 2D-DCT coefficients of that moment tensor, updated via EMA in the transform domain every step (cheap: a truncated DCT is O(d log d) via row/column separable transforms, or done every M steps on a subsampled matrix to save compute); the Adam denominator used for the actual parameter update is a blend of the elementwise moment and the inverse-DCT reconstruction from the low-frequency coefficients, weighted to fall back to pure elementwise on early steps. Only the DCT basis and blend weight are new; everything else in Adam is unchanged, and this is trained end-to-end as part of normal optimisation (no separate training phase).
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification: the elementwise (vanilla Adam) moment is retained in full alongside the spectral compressed version, so the run can be validated against a pure-Adam control path and reverted per-parameter if the spectral reconstruction is a poor predictor of the true elementwise moment (checked periodically via reconstruction error threshold).

falsifier.hypothesis: Blending elementwise Adam moments with a low-frequency spectral reconstruction of the moment matrix improves convergence speed or final loss at matched FLOPs+params versus vanilla Adam, by exploiting structured (low-rank/smooth) curvature across a weight matrix.
falsifier.metric: training loss / perplexity at fixed step budget; wall-clock overhead of DCT maintenance; reconstruction error of spectral vs elementwise moments over training
falsifier.baseline: vanilla Adam, and Shampoo/K-FAC as a stronger structured-preconditioner baseline
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2/llama preset, paperkiln, 12 seeds, matched FLOPs with DCT overhead counted, 40 GPU-hour budget, ablate number of retained low-frequency coefficients

name: Graph-propagated optimiser moments
claim: Graph-message-passing applied to optimiser-state so that per-parameter moment estimates are updated using averaged/gated signals from structurally adjacent parameters (same layer, same head, residual-stream neighbors) instead of being estimated in isolation.
new_capability: The optimiser can share second-moment/variance information across parameters that co-occur in a module (e.g. all weights feeding one attention head), giving faster-converging, lower-variance step sizes for under-sampled parameters without changing the model architecture.
placement: Define a static graph over parameter tensors (edges: same-layer, same-head, adjacent-layer residual links) once at init from the model config. Every optimiser step, after computing raw Adam-style m,v per parameter, run one round of message passing (weighted average with learned or fixed edge weights) over v (and optionally m) before applying the update; this adds O(E) extra ops per step, trained jointly with the model (edge weights, if learned, updated by a separate small optimizer or fixed as 1/degree). Implemented as a wrapper around the existing optimiser in paperkiln's C++ trainer, operating only on optimiser state tensors, not model forward/backward.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the message-passing overhead is a small fixed optimiser-side cost added identically to baseline and treatment, and model parameter count is untouched, so comparisons are at matched model FLOPs/params (extra optimiser compute is reported separately and kept negligible).

name: renormalised optimiser moments

claim: Hopfield content-addressed retrieval applied to optimiser-state so that a bank of stored final second-moment patterns from prior training runs can be recalled by energy descent, keyed on the current model's early-training moment pattern, to warm-start optimiser state on a new but related run.

name: Hebbian fast-weight context compression
claim: Hebbian outer-product fast-weight memory applied to the context window so that low-contribution positions decay out of an associative store within a few steps instead of occupying a fixed KV slot for their full lifetime in the window.
new_capability: The model can effectively 'forget' tokens that stop being predictive within a short horizon, freeing capacity for new tokens without hitting the hard context-length ceiling, giving variable effective retention instead of uniform per-position cost.
placement: Maintain a fixed-size fast-weight matrix A (dxd) updated at every token by a decayed outer-product rule A_t = lambda*A_{t-1} + eta * v_t k_t^T using the current token's key/value; queries read from A via a matrix-vector product added as an extra term to standard attention logits/values. This runs alongside (not replacing) a shortened sliding-window exact-attention lane; A and its read/write projections are trained jointly from scratch at matched budget. Update happens every token; decay rate lambda is a trained or swept scalar.
invariant: outputs stay causal; the fast-weight state at time t is a function only of tokens up to t, and reads at time t only use A_{t-1} or A_t computed from past tokens.

falsifier.hypothesis: Hebbian fast-weight augmentation lets a model with a short sliding window (e.g. 256) match or beat a plain exact-attention model with the full window (e.g. 1024) on a matched-FLOPs budget, on tasks needing medium-range recall.
falsifier.metric: perplexity and associative-recall accuracy (synthetic key-value retrieval task at varying lag)
falsifier.baseline: sliding-window attention alone with the same short window and matched FLOPs (no fast weights), and full exact-attention window as upper-bound reference
falsifier.protocol: nano llama preset, window 256 vs 1024, 12 seeds, fast-weight dim = model dim, decay swept in {0.9,0.95,0.99}, matched total FLOPs by adjusting depth/width

nearest_known: Fast Weight Programmers (Schmidhuber 1992; Schlag & Schmidhuber 2021 linear-transformer fast weights), Recurrent Memory Transformer
