name: Choquet head aggregation
claim: Choquet-integral aggregation with pairwise interaction terms applied to multi-head attention output combination so that heads are weighted by a learned fuzzy measure capturing redundancy/complementarity instead of being summed independently.
new_capability: The model can down-weight redundant head pairs and up-weight complementary ones per-token, at inference realizing an adaptive effective head count instead of always combining all heads with fixed (often just-concatenation) weights.
placement: Replace the standard concat+linear head-merge with: for each token, compute per-head scalar 'contribution' scores, then aggregate them via a discrete Choquet integral under a 2-additive capacity mu (one scalar singleton weight per head plus one pairwise interaction weight per head-pair, monotonicity enforced via a softplus reparameterization). This aggregation module (capacity parameters: H singleton + H(H-1)/2 pairwise, negligible extra params) is trained jointly with the rest of the network from scratch at matched budget; computed every forward pass, every layer.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the Choquet layer adds O(H^2) scalar parameters and O(H log H) sort-based computation per token, negligible relative to attention compute, so budget stays matched by trimming elsewhere (e.g. slightly reduced FFN width) to equalize total FLOPs.

falsifier.metric: validation perplexity; head-redundancy metric (change in loss under single-head ablation, pre/post)
falsifier.baseline: standard multi-head concat + linear merge, width-adjusted to match total params/FLOPs
falsifier.protocol: nano gpt2 preset, 8 heads, 12 seeds, capacity monotonicity enforced via projected gradient, matched FLOPs by param budget accounting

nearest_known: attention head importance / pruning literature (Michel et al. 2019 'Are Sixteen Heads Really Better than One'), gating/mixture-of-heads mechanisms; Choquet integral itself is novel in this slot
deficit: heads are always all on; there is no routing among heads

name: Submodular greedy head selection
claim: Greedy submodular maximization applied to multi-head attention so that only a diminishing-returns-guaranteed subset of heads is activated per token/layer instead of always running all heads.

name: Sinkhorn head-token routing
claim: Optimal-transport Sinkhorn matching applied to multi-head attention so that heads are assigned to tokens (or token-groups) via a balanced doubly-stochastic routing plan instead of every head attending to every token uniformly.
new_capability: The model can enforce balanced, differentiable soft-routing of specific heads to specific tokens/positions (avoiding both head collapse and uniform all-on heads), giving controllable head-specialization with a load-balance guarantee absent from vanilla multi-head attention.

The cost-function parameters and head embeddings are trained jointly from scratch at matched budget; Sinkhorn iterations run every forward pass per layer (cheap, O(H*T*iters)).

name: Thompson-sampled head router
claim: Thompson sampling applied to multi-head attention so that each token position routes to a stochastically-sampled subset of heads chosen from a posterior over per-head value rather than always activating all heads deterministically.

name: MDL-selected head subset

name: PQ-shared KV cache pool
claim: Product-quantisation applied to the serving-batch's per-request KV caches so that structurally similar prefixes across concurrent requests share compressed cache entries instead of storing full-precision K/V independently.

Attention reads reconstruct approximate K/V from codebook indices; exact K/V are kept in a small recent-window buffer (sink/sliding-window lane) so recency-critical attention stays exact.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification; the exact K/V for the recent window is retained and codebook approximation error is bounded and checked against a threshold, falling back to exact storage for any subvector whose quantisation error exceeds it.

name: multi-scale coarse-grained shared cache
claim: renormalisation-group applied to serving-batch so that KV states from many independent requests are coarse-grained into a hierarchy of shared summaries at increasing context-scale, and requests read the coarsest summary that still changes their output within tolerance
new_capability: the server can serve arbitrarily many independent requests against a shared multi-scale 'background' representation (e.g. common-domain long-range statistics) whose fine detail is only recomputed per-request when it actually matters for that request's prediction, instead of every request paying full-resolution cost for context it doesn't need to resolve finely

(like RG decimation) to build a pyramid of coarsened shared context representations, trained/fit via reconstruction loss so each scale predicts the next-finer scale's aggregate statistics; at serving time each request attends to the coarsest level first and only unrolls to finer levels for positions where the coarse read's predicted next-token distribution disagrees with a finer-scale probe above a KL threshold. This is a from-scratch auxiliary module trained separately from the base LM on activation traces, not touching base model weights.
invariant: exactness is recoverable: the finest scale is exactly the base model's own KV cache, so any request can always unroll to full resolution and recover the exact baseline output; the coarse levels are only ever used as a fast pre-filter with a verified fallback

name: LSH-bucketed KV cache sharing
claim: Locality-sensitive hashing applied to serving-batch request states so that similar prompt/context prefixes across concurrent requests can share cached KV computation instead of recomputing independently.
new_capability: The serving batch can detect and exploit cross-request redundancy (near-duplicate prefixes, common system prompts, repeated retrieval contexts) to cut redundant compute at inference time, which an independent-requests batcher cannot do by construction.
placement: At batch-formation time, hash a rolling window (e.g. last 64-128 tokens) of each request's hidden-state or token-id sequence with a fixed LSH family (e.g. SimHash over embedding projections); requests whose current-window hash matches an existing bucket are pointed at that bucket's stored KV segment instead of computing their own, with a per-token verification check (exact match of the underlying token ids, not just hash collision) before reuse is allowed. This is a serving-time/inference-time mechanism only: no base model retraining, just an added cache-lookup-and-copy path plus a small hash-projection matrix that can be fit once on held-out data. Recomputation happens whenever the verification check fails, falling back to the independent path.
invariant: exactness recoverable by verification

name: PID-controlled router balancing
claim: feedback-control applied to the moe-router so that expert load balances via a closed-loop controller instead of a competing auxiliary loss
new_capability: The router can maintain target load balance without a fixed-weight auxiliary loss term fighting the task gradient, allowing the balance/quality tradeoff to be tuned online rather than fixed at design time.
placement: At every training step (or every k=8 steps to reduce overhead), compute per-expert load error e_i = target_fraction - observed_fraction (EMA over a window of ~256 tokens). Maintain integral and derivative terms per expert and add a bias b_i = Kp*e_i + Ki*sum(e_i) + Kd*d(e_i)/dt directly to the router logits before top-k selection, instead of adding a load-balancing loss to the total objective. Only the PID gains (3 scalars, shared across experts) and the routing weights are trained; the controller state (integral, derivative accumulators) is not a learned parameter but an online-updated buffer logged to events.jsonl.
invariant: matched FLOPs/params; the PID bias is computed from cheap scalar statistics and added to logits, no extra parameters or forward passes versus the aux-loss baseline.

falsifier.hypothesis: PID-controlled logit bias reaches the same expert-load balance (max/min expert fraction ratio < 1.5) as the standard aux-loss MoE at equal or better validation loss, using fewer total gradient-conflicting loss terms.
falsifier.metric: validation perplexity at matched load-balance ratio, and variance of expert load over training
falsifier.baseline: standard top-k MoE with switch-transformer-style auxiliary load balancing loss, matched FLOPs/params
falsifier.protocol: nano-scale gpt2 preset with 8 experts top-2, 12 seeds, matched token budget, sweep PID gains on 2 seeds then lock for remaining 10, measure final perplexity and load variance over training curve

name: Hebbian fast-weight FFN memory
claim: hebbian-fast-weights applied to the ffn so that the key-value memory it implements can be rewritten by the current stream within a context window instead of staying fixed post-training
new_capability: The model can bind and later retrieve token-specific associations introduced mid-sequence (e.g. a novel name-to-fact pairing given once in-context) without gradient updates, which a fixed FFN cannot do by construction.
placement: Augment each FFN block's first weight matrix W1 with a low-rank fast-weight term A_t built from a decaying sum of outer products of recent hidden states and their FFN activations: A_t = lambda*A_{t-1} + eta*(h_t outer phi(h_t)), decayed over a window of ~64-128 tokens; the effective weight used per token is W1 + A_t, applied causally so A_t at position t only uses h_{<=t}. Only lambda, eta and a small low-rank projection are trained (base W1, W2 stay frozen after pretraining or trained jointly at matched budget, stated as from-scratch matched-budget run); A_t itself is never gradient-trained, it is recomputed by the fixed Hebbian rule at every forward pass, streaming.
invariant: outputs remain causal; A_t at position t is built only from h_{<=t}, and streaming holds because A_t is updated incrementally token by token without revisiting future tokens.

falsifier.hypothesis: Adding Hebbian fast-weights to the FFN improves in-context associative recall (synthetic key-value binding task inserted mid-sequence, queried later in the same sequence) over a matched-FLOPs static-FFN baseline, at equal held-out language-modeling perplexity.
falsifier.metric: recall accuracy on synthetic bound-pair retrieval task at varying distance (16/64/256 tokens), plus held-out perplexity delta
falsifier.baseline: matched-FLOPs/params static FFN transformer (llama-nano preset) with no fast-weight term
falsifier.protocol: from-scratch matched-budget training, 12 seeds, synthetic associative-recall eval interleaved with natural text, sweep lambda/eta on 2 seeds then lock
